job.title: Business Development Manager | Medical Technologies
job.description:
THE COMPANY YOU WOULD BE JOINING
  • This global medical device company has been delivering medical technologies for life saving procedures since 2016.
  • Their research & development team, based in the USA, works with specialist doctors on innovative solutions, pioneering devices to transform the lives of patients.
SOME OF THE BENEFITS TO YOU
  • They create an extraordinary employee experience goes beyond benefits and perks.
  • They are building a company committed to the care of each employee’s professional and personal success.
  • They strive to create an environment where talented individuals can inspire unique solutions to meaningful problems.
THE ROLE – WHAT YOU WILL LEAD & GROW
  • This Territory Manager position looking after Sydney's South, NSW will build deep, long-lasting relationships with hospitals and clinicians through providing clinical demonstrations and instruction for use of company products in presale, implementation, and post-sale situations in formal educational as well as small group or individual presentations in patient-care areas throughout a healthcare facility, to gain or increase acceptance of company’s products and technology.
  • This is a hunter sales position. You will sell to emergency physicians, interventional radiologists and vascular surgeons and provide case support within the operating theatre, supporting surgeons in the use of your product. This role is on-call 1 in every 3 weeks, however, it is rare to be called out outside of normal business hours and you will work in a team so will have support.
  • This is a strategic senior sales role that requires you to develop a clinical pathway for doctors and surgeons to understand how and why the use of your product is essential for best patient outcomes.
  • The role will work with customers & prospects to introduce, promote, and increase the usage of products throughout a hospital and assist with the collection and dissemination of information or feedback provided by customers.
  • You will represent the company at various trade shows or educational meetings and provide product support and education to users primarily in hospitals, specialist rooms or theatre.
  • You will continuously increase knowledge of new developments within your territory as well as company products to perform as a subject matter expert.
WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO GET THE JOB
  • Bachelor of Science degree or related qualification.
  • Medical device sales experience (5+ years) selling medical devices to surgeons within the operating theatre environment with a deep understanding of the hospital landscape in NSW Health, preferably working with interventional radiologists and/or vascular surgeons, however, this is not mandatory. The right attitude and medical device surgical sales in the OR is key here.
  • Acceptance of a on-call clinical support (in theatre) component (keeping in mind this does not occur often, 1 in every 3 weeks and the load is shared with the NSW team).
  • Strategic sales background as a senior medical device sales rep used to navigating the internal machinations of NSW Health hospitals to develop clinical pathways for product uptake. 
  • Ability to work independently with little or no direct supervision.
  • Advanced MS Office skills to develop effective reports, spreadsheets, and presentations.
  • Demonstrate effective educational and presentation skills in diverse settings from one-on-one to formal large group situations.
  • You will have full Australian working rights and be vaccinated against Covid.
Interested?
Please 'apply now' or call Scott Della-Pietra on 0416.021.937. quoting reference number 3919. Please note, your details/resume will not be sent anywhere without a formal interview and, if successful, your subsequent prior permission. Personal information provided will be used for recruitment purposes only and be treated in the strictest confidence. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

job.title: Territory Manager | Medical Devices
job.description:
THE COMPANY YOU WOULD BE JOINING
  • This medical device company has been supporting surgeons, doctors and clinicians for over 60 years and has grown into a worldwide manufacturer and distributor of some of the best medical technology in their niche space.
  • This organisation combines their expertise in medical devices with software solutions to achieve integration in the operating theatre environment and to support clinical procedures and resource management.
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU
  • This company offers you amazing opportunities to actually make an impact.
  • They consistently challenge and support their people’s personal and professional development.
  • They are always interested in recruiting great people to enable them to continue to play a pioneering role as a leading manufacturer of medical devices and medical technology.
WHAT YOU WILL LEAD AND GROW
  • This Territory Manager role will generate and acquire new business and maximise sales objectives through direct customers and meet customer and territory KPI’s.
  • The position is responsible for selling and promoting a range of devices and consumables to hospitals (sometimes within theatre, but NO on-call), within Brisbane CBD & surrounds with weekly trips to Toowoomba.

  • Due to the nature of your role and level of responsibility, participation and attendance at events, seminars, exhibitions or workshops will require attendance on some weekends and evenings as necessary (on occasion).

job.title: Senior Biomedical Engineer | Medical Devices
job.description:
THE COMPANY YOU WOULD BE JOINING
  • This medical device company has been supporting surgeons, doctors and clinicians for over 60 years and has grown into a worldwide manufacturer and distributor of some of the best medical technology in their niche space.
  • This organisation combines their expertise in medical devices with software solutions to achieve integration in the operating theatre environment and to support clinical procedures and resource management.
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU
  • This company offers you amazing opportunities to actually make an impact.
  • They consistently challenge and support their people’s personal and professional development.
  • They are always interested in recruiting great people to enable them to continue to play a pioneering role as a leading manufacturer of medical devices and medical technology.
WHAT YOU WILL LEAD AND GROW
  • This Senior Biomedical Engineer position, based in Auckland, NZ is responsible for managing the end-to-end service and operational delivery of biomedical equipment across New Zealand, including overseeing the NZ workshop and ensuring the full-service lifecycle for customer accounts is delivered efficiently and to a high standard.
  • The role involves performing complex technical repairs and maintenance, while also handling administrative and logistical aspects of service operations, operating with a high degree of independence in daily decision-making. The manager of this role is based in Sydney.
  • The position will oversee the day-to-day operations of the New Zealand workshop, including equipment intake, job prioritisation, and maintaining an organised and efficient workspace, along with maintaining accurate and up-to-date service records, job tracking, and work orders within SAP and the Quality Management System, ensuring all documentation is audit-ready at all times.
  • You will inspect, test, and repair loan and demonstration equipment to ensure availability meets the needs of the sales and customer teams and drive a proactive and strategic approach to asset lifecycle management by identifying aging equipment, prioritising service or replacement needs, and aligning actions with customer requirements and service contract commitments.
  • You will conduct safety and performance testing of equipment in compliance with applicable regulatory standards, including ANZ 3551, and internal company requirements and deliver both preventative maintenance and responsive repair services across the New Zealand hospital customer base to ensure optimal equipment performance and reliability.
  • You will diagnose and resolve complex technical issues independently, escalating where necessary to ensure timely and effective resolution and install and validate software updates, manage system integrations, and troubleshoot related issues to maintain and enhance overall equipment functionality and performance.
  • You will apply sound knowledge of hospital and surgical environments, including relevant standards such as AS/NZS 3551 and AS/NZS 3200 and demonstrate working knowledge of ISO 13485 and its application within medical device servicing and quality processes.
WHAT EXPERIENCE & SKILLS WILL YOU NEED TO GET THE JOB?
  • A degree or diploma in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 5+ years’ experience in biomedical engineering or a medical device service role in the medical device industry.
  • EWRB registration (EST/Electrician) with MCPA endorsement, or willingness to obtain.
  • Experience in the installation, maintenance, and servicing of capital medical equipment.
  • Exposure to laser equipment, particularly in testing and validation, is highly desirable, but not mandatory.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and manage a regional workload with minimal supervision.
  • A full, current New Zealand driver’s licence and legal eligibility to work in New Zealand.
  • Strong technical troubleshooting, diagnostic and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience working within hospital/clinical environments and relevant medical device quality standards.

job.title: Quality Engineer | MedTech
job.description:
THE COMPANY YOU WOULD BE JOINING
  • This Australian med-tech start-up, established 9 years ago, is working to improve women’s health, leveraging AI-enabled technology to reinvent care for women.
  • They utilise cutting edge platforms and create completely novel technologies to generate solutions that seek to treat complications that have been previously undiagnosable. 
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS
  • This organisation prides themselves on being an extremely flexible workplace, with a focus on outcomes, rather than location or hours.
  • The company offers a uniquely supportive environment for learning, as well as opportunities for growth for high performers.
  • You will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience and develop your knowledge, while creating groundbreaking solutions that truly make a difference to women’s health.
THE OPPORTUNITY – WHAT YOU WILL LEAD & GROW
  • This Quality Engineer position will directly influence how quality is built into their products, processes, and culture. Joining at an exciting stage of growth, this role will help design, implement, and continuously improve the Quality Management System, ensuring it remains scalable, compliant, and aligned with the business needs.
  • This is a highly collaborative role requiring close partnership across Engineering, Clinical, Manufacturing and Product. You will contribute across all aspects of the QMS, including certification activities and regulatory submissions along with design, manufacturing and post market activities. This role is critical to ensure we deliver safe, effective, and innovative products.
  • The position will support quality planning, including leading some workstreams, to achieve and maintain site certification and review relevant standards, regulations and guidance and incorporate into the QMS as needed.
  • The role will draft, review and implement new or updated QMS procedures and work instructions by working closely with cross functional team members and represent Quality Assurance on design projects including new products and design changes.
  • You will implement and maintain Quality Plans and Compliance reviews and provide constructive review and approval on key documents and plans.
  • You will act as QA/QC representative for manufacturing activities, including process and software validation and conduct internal and supplier audits and support external audits and ensure appropriate audit documentation and close out of deficiencies.
  • You will manage suppliers, create and maintain the approved supplier list and quality agreements, and support ongoing performance assessments.
  • You will manage, handle and review nonconformances, complaints, other product quality issues and CAPAs.
  • You will perform investigations and root cause analysis, develop and implement corrective and preventative actions in collaboration with other departments and lead or support core Quality Assurance activities including training, document and record control.
WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO GET THE JOB
  • Engineering university qualification.
  • Demonstrated experience working in medical devices and applying the requirements of ISO13485, 21 CFR Part 820 and Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP). Strong knowledge of global regulatory requirements, including FDA and TGA.
  • Broad experience across Quality Management Systems including design, manufacturing and post market activities.
  • Experience with medical devices incorporating software, electronics and mechanical components.
  • Strong understanding and application of risk management according to ISO14971. Quality audit training and experience.
  • Practical experience authoring QMS and audit-ready documents for design files, quality records and regulatory submissions.
  • Strong English communication, written and verbal, with full Australian working rights and ability to collaborate effectively with cross functional teams, with work experience in Australia.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and leading resolution of risks and implementation of product quality improvements.
  • Solid understanding or experience with Machine Learning principles.
  • Prior experience implementing a QMS.

job.title: Head of Finance
job.description:
THE COMPANY YOU WOULD BE JOINING
  • This global medical company specialises in products and services that are used to help care for chronically ill patients.
  • They are committed to putting medical technologies in the hands of people who help improve patient outcomes.
WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING DAY TO DAY
  • This role will suit a commercially astute Head of Finance to join the senior leadership team of an established healthcare organisation operating across Australia and New Zealand.
  • This is a broad leadership role with responsibility for the financial performance, governance and commercial stewardship of the business, while also contributing to the development and execution of broader organisational strategy.
  • Working closely with the Managing Director and senior leadership team, the Finance Director will provide high-level financial insight, challenge and guidance to support sustainable growth, investment decisions and overall business performance.
  • Key responsibilities will include:
  • Partnering with the Managing Director and leadership team to support strategic planning, commercial decision making and business growth.
  • Providing meaningful financial analysis and advice to assess opportunities, investments, risks and operational performance.
  • Leading the annual budgeting, forecasting and financial planning processes across the Australia and New Zealand businesses.
  • Monitoring financial performance against agreed targets and providing regular reporting and commentary to senior leadership.
  • Working closely with business leaders to maintain strong cost management disciplines and ensure expenditure is aligned with organisational priorities.
  • Establishing and monitoring working capital objectives, including receivables, inventory and supplier payments.
  • Ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting to local, regional and group stakeholders.
  • Maintaining strong financial controls, governance frameworks and administrative processes across the business.
  • Overseeing statutory reporting requirements and ensuring compliance with relevant accounting, taxation and regulatory obligations.
  • Managing relationships with external auditors and coordinating the annual audit process.
  • Overseeing corporate taxation requirements, including GST, FBT, income tax and other relevant statutory obligations.
  • Providing oversight of treasury, cash flow and broader financial risk management activities.
  • Providing leadership, direction and development to the Finance team, ensuring capability and processes continue to evolve with the business.
YOU WILL HAVE THE FOLLOWING TO BE SUCCESSFUL
  • Extensive senior finance experience, including substantial responsibility for leading a finance function within a sizeable, commercially focused organisation.
  • Experience operating in a complex business environment with meaningful scale, ideally within an organisation generating significant annual revenue.
  • You must have recently worked for a manufacturer as opposed to a service organisation.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in accounting, finance, commerce or a related discipline, with CPA, CA or equivalent professional accreditation.
  • Experience with taxation and financial reporting obligations within Australia & ideally NZ with US GAAP knowledge.
  • Strong financial systems capability, with experience using enterprise-level ERP platforms such as SAP and confidence across the Microsoft Office suite.
  • A proactive and solutions-oriented approach, with the ability to identify issues early, exercise sound judgement and develop practical responses without requiring close direction.
  • The ability to move comfortably between high-level strategic thinking and detailed operational execution when required.
  • Strong commercial instincts and the confidence to contribute beyond the traditional finance remit to broader organisational priorities and decision making.
  • A collaborative, energetic and self-directed working style, supported by strong relationship-building, communication and influencing skills.
  • The maturity and interpersonal capability to work effectively with senior executives, operational leaders and cross-functional teams.
